statement: Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns a result r, r is the minimum over all colorings c of length n with 0 <= c[i] < k for every 0 <= i < n and c[i] != c[i+1] for every 0 <= i < n-1, of the total cost sum_{i=0}^{n-1} costs[i][c[i]]; that is, r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} costs[i][c[i]] for every such coloring c, and r = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} costs[i][c*[i]] for at least one such coloring c*.
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.

statement: The function min_cost_ii(costs) returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access costs out of bounds for any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.

statement: Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns a result r, there exists a coloring c of length n with 0 <= c[i] < k for every 0 <= i < n and c[i] != c[i+1] for every 0 <= i < n-1, such that r = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} costs[i][c[i]].
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.

statement: Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns a result r, for every coloring c of length n with 0 <= c[i] < k for every 0 <= i < n and c[i] != c[i+1] for every 0 <= i < n-1, we have r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} costs[i][c[i]].
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.

statement: Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns a result r, r >= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (min_{0 <= j < k} costs[i][j]).
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.

statement: Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns a result r, r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (max_{0 <= j < k} costs[i][j]).
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.

statement: Let pi be a permutation of {0,1,...,k-1}. Define costs_pi with the same dimensions by costs_pi[i][j] = costs[i][pi(j)] for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k. Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns r and min_cost_ii(costs_pi) returns r_pi, we have r_pi = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.

statement: Define costs_rev by costs_rev[i][j] = costs[n-1-i][j] for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k. Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns r and min_cost_ii(costs_rev) returns r_rev, we have r_rev = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.

statement: Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns r and min_cost_ii(costs2) returns r2, we have r2 = r + d.
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k. Let costs2 be another matrix with len(costs2) = n, len(costs2[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs2[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k. Fix an index i0 with 0 <= i0 < n, and suppose there is an integer d such that costs2[i0][j] = costs[i0][j] + d for every 0 <= j < k, and costs2[i][j] = costs[i][j] for every i != i0 and every 0 <= j < k.

statement: Whenever min_cost_ii(costs) returns r and min_cost_ii(costs2) returns r2, we have r2 >= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(costs) and k = len(costs[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 100, 2 <= k <= 20, len(costs[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, and 1 <= costs[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k. Let costs2 be another matrix with len(costs2) = n, len(costs2[i]) = k for every 0 <= i < n, 1 <= costs2[i][j] <= 20 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k, and costs2[i][j] >= costs[i][j] for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < k.
